company_name: Hitachi Construction Machinery Co., Ltd. (renaming to LANDCROS Corporation, April 2027)

inputs.sbc_source: Kessan tanshin FY ended Mar-2026, consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payment transactions' JPY 95m (JPY 104m prior year). No separate equity-award tax line; Japan is an SBC-zero market for this filer.
inputs.buyback_note: JPY 30,573m 'Payments for purchase of treasury stock' in H1 FY2027 (Apr-Sep 2026) financing activities; FY2026 full year was JPY 6m. Treasury shares rose 2.38m -> 7.74m. The reduction is already in the 207.373m share count; no further buyback is modelled and the count is held flat.
inputs.share_count_basis: 215,115,038 issued less 7,741,957 treasury at 2026-09-30 (H1 FY2027 tanshin) = 207,373,081. No dilutive instruments of substance (basic EPS = diluted EPS; SBC JPY 0.1bn/yr). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (at ~0%), and no non-SBC issuance is planned.
inputs.fy_label_note: Metrics CSV labels fiscal years by the March year-end (FY2026 = year ended 31 Mar 2026). The company's own documents call the same year 'FY2025' and the filing is named 6305.T_Annual_FY2025.txt. Forecast year here = FY2027 = year ending 31 Mar 2027.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T06:30:00Z (TSE regular close; Yahoo Finance chart API). Regular session print, not after-hours.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bonds and borrowings 311,023 current + 176,720 non-current = 487,743 less cash and cash equivalents 118,999, all at 2026-09-30 (H1 FY2027 tanshin). Lease liabilities (13,915 + 60,933 = 74,848) are NOT in total_debt; they are deducted once in equity_bridge (lease treatment A).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. Cost of equity ~9.0%: 10y JGB ~1.7% + beta 1.25 (global construction/mining equipment cyclical) x ERP 5.8%. After-tax cost of debt ~2.2% (FY2026 interest paid JPY 16.0bn on ~JPY 520bn average borrowings = 3.1% pre-tax; mix of JPY and overseas-currency borrowings). Target weights 75/25 equity/debt (the company's own net D/E target is ~0.3-0.4x; current market-value weights of 64/36 reflect a de-rated equity) -> 7.3%, rounded to 7.5%. The SAME WACC is used for all three scenarios: cyclicality, FX and tariff risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) - leases as debt. IFRS 16 filer. Lease payments (JPY 13,479m principal FY2026) are NOT deducted inside EBITDA; lease liabilities JPY 74,848m (2026-09-30) are deducted once in equity_bridge; the renewal of lease assets is charged through capex_pct_path, which carries ~1.0pp of revenue for lease-asset renewal (principal payments 13.5bn / revenue 1,405bn = 0.96%) on top of ~3.5-3.8pp of PP&E + intangible capex. D&A is left post-IFRS-16 (includes right-of-use depreciation), which is consistent with charging the renewal as capex.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: non-controlling interests (Tata Hitachi, HCM China, Bradken-related and other partly-owned subsidiaries; book JPY 53,053m at 2026-09-30) take 11.3-11.5% of consolidated net income every year FY2024-FY2026 (9,495 / 82,688 in FY2026). The NCI share is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined leakage rate: 1 - (1 - 0.33 cash tax) x (1 - 0.115 NCI) = 40.7%, carried as 40.5%. The NCI stock is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. Calibration: FY2026 adjusted operating income 132,951 x (1 - 0.405) = 79.1bn vs attributable net income 73,193 + after-tax net financial expense ~6.4bn - equity-method income ~2.4bn = 77.2bn: ties within non-operating noise. FY2027 guidance ties too: pretax 150,000 x 0.595 = 89.3bn vs guided attributable 90,000.
inputs.non_operating_assets_note: Equity-method investments (JPY 30,551m book, 2026-09-30) are added in equity_bridge because their income (JPY 3.6bn FY2026) sits below adjusted operating income and is excluded from the flows. Interest and dividend income (JPY 5.6bn + 2.6bn FY2026) are likewise outside adjusted operating income; their source (cash) is already in net debt, so interest_income is left at 0 - the company is net-debt, not net-cash, so the owner-fcf.md section 1(b) strip does not apply. 'Other financial assets' (JPY 32.8bn current + 36.5bn non-current) are a mix of derivatives, deposits, loans and securities without a clean fair-value split in the tanshin; not added (conservative).
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer: trade receivables 258bn + 45bn non-current + inventories 563bn - payables 231bn = ~635bn net operating working capital at 2026-09-30, 42% of FY2027 revenue. wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (growth consumes cash). Set at -30% rather than the full 42% because part of receivables are debt-funded retail-finance receivables and the company is running an inventory-turn reduction programme (inventories released 51.8bn in FY2026, 29.4bn in FY2025).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md. Hitachi Construction Machinery is the world's #3 hydraulic-excavator and a top-tier mining-truck/ultra-large-excavator maker (Komatsu and Caterpillar are the peers); ~30% of revenue is mining, ~44% is parts & service / rental / used ('value chain'). FY0 is FY2026 (year ended 31 Mar 2026): revenue 1,405,493, adjusted operating income 132,951 (9.5%), statutory operating income 130,144, D&A 77,853, capex 40,968 + intangibles 8,065, attributable net income 73,193. The forecast year FY2027 is anchored to the UPWARDLY REVISED guidance in the H1 FY2027 tanshin (2026-10/11): revenue 1,500,000, adjusted operating income 155,000 (10.3%), attributable net income 90,000, EPS 430.14, at JPY 154/USD from Q3; dividend JPY 190. CYCLE WARNING: FY2027 guidance is a near-peak year - revenue has run 1.37-1.5tn for four years on a weak yen, adjusted OP margin ranged 4.0% (FY2021 trough) to 12.0% (FY2024 peak) over the cycle. The base case therefore does NOT extrapolate FY2027: it models a mid-cycle correction in FY2028-FY2029 and settles at a 15% EBITDA margin (~9.5-10% adjusted OP), the FY2019-FY2026 average, and the terminal value is capped at 15x FCF (cyclical cap), which binds in every scenario. House and street bases coincide (SBC ~0%) so band_position is null. Discounting end-of-year, 10-year explicit horizon so the margin path has matured before capitalisation. Everything in JPY millions; price in JPY.

equity_bridge.item: Lease liabilities (IFRS 16) treated as debt - current 13,915 + non-current 60,933 at 2026-09-30
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2027 tanshin consolidated balance sheet; treatment (A), see inputs.lease_treatment

equity_bridge.item: Investments accounted for using the equity method, at book
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2027 tanshin balance sheet 2026-09-30; income from these is excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal growth for a global construction/mining equipment maker (global excavator demand ~flat, price + parts & service mix growth), well below the cycle-inflated equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.8% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 47.9% and sits with revenue 11.6%; all 5-year CAGRs run from the FY2021 COVID trough (revenue 813bn, EPS JPY 48.62) to a near-peak FY2026 and overstate trend growth. The 3-year CAGRs (revenue 3.2%, EPS 1.4%) are the better guide and are what the base case converges to.
historical_growth.notes: FCF series is owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC of ~JPY 0.1bn; interest income not stripped because the company is net-debt). 3-year FCF CAGR is undefined: FY2023 owner FCF was -78,974 (inventory build). Reported FCF is dominated by working-capital swings (-51.9bn FY2019, -79.0bn FY2023, +123.3bn FY2026 on a 51.8bn inventory release), which is why the forward build is component-based and not a carry-forward of the FY2026 margin. SBC is immaterial so the SBC-adjusted and reported CAGRs are identical.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = revised FY2027 guidance (1,500bn, +6.7%, helped by JPY 154/USD). FY2028-29 models the mid-cycle correction the company itself flags (excavator and mining demand slightly down, yen tailwind fading): -4%, -2%. Recovery +3/+4%, then 3% fading to 2% nominal. 10-year CAGR ~2.0%, consistent with selected_growth_rate 2.5% less a cycle haircut.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA = adjusted operating income + D&A. Y1 15.7% = guided adjusted OP 10.3% + D&A 5.4%. Dips to 13% in the correction (adjusted OP ~7.8%, between the FY2021 4% trough and mid-cycle) and settles at 15% (adjusted OP ~10%), the FY2019-FY2026 average of ~9.5-10% plus the parts & service mix shift.
base.tax_rationale: 40.5% = 33% cash tax (FY2026 cash tax paid 41,478 / pretax 124,226 = 33.4%; FY2025 35%) combined with 11.5% NCI leakage; see inputs.nci_treatment.
base.capex_rationale: PP&E + intangibles 3.5% (FY2026 49.0bn; FY2024 4.2%, FY2025 3.3%) plus ~1.0% lease-asset renewal, drifting to 4.8% as D&A converges to 5.0%.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 7.5%/2.0% implies 18.5x FCF; the 15x cyclical cap binds. 15x year-10 FCF equates to ~5.5x year-10 EBITDA, inside the stock's own 5-8x EV/EBITDA history.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2027 beats the revised guidance (+8%); no FY2028-29 correction - North American and copper/gold mining demand hold, Indonesia/coal weakness is offset, yen stays 150+. Growth then 4% fading to 2%.
bull.margin_rationale: Adjusted OP margin sustained at 11-11.5% (FY2024 peak was 12.0%) on parts & service mix, pricing and the completed Deere-dealer-exit restructuring in the Americas; EBITDA 16-16.5%.

bear.growth_rationale: H2 FY2027 falls short (Middle East logistics, tariffs, JPY strengthens toward 140) so FY2027 is +3%; then a real downturn: -10% and -6% (FY2020-21 fell 10% then 13%) as coal/iron-ore mining capex stalls and North American construction rolls over; slow recovery.
bear.margin_rationale: EBITDA 10-11% at the trough = adjusted OP ~4.5-5.5% (FY2021 was 4.0%), recovering only to 14% (adjusted OP ~9%) as tariffs and brand-change costs stick. D&A rises as a % of a smaller revenue base; capex cut but not below maintenance.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands on the twice-raised guidance (revenue 1.5tn, adjusted OP 155bn, attributable NI 90bn) with the weak yen and North American excavator strength doing the work. The cycle then turns: global excavator demand drifts down, mining fleet replacement pauses in Indonesia and coal/iron ore while copper and gold hold, and the yen gives back part of its tailwind, so FY2028-29 revenue falls ~6% cumulatively and adjusted OP margin dips toward 8%. The parts & service / rental 'value chain' (44% of revenue, growing every year since FY2021) cushions the downturn and lifts the mid-cycle adjusted OP margin to ~10% (EBITDA 15%) by FY2031. Capex runs ~4.6-4.8% of revenue including lease renewal, working capital consumes 30% of each yen of growth, and 11.5% of earnings leak to Tata Hitachi and other minorities. The LANDCROS rebrand (April 2027) is a cost, not a driver. Terminal value capped at 15x FCF, the cyclical cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: No correction. North American construction and infrastructure demand stays at FY2026 levels, copper/gold mining capex offsets coal weakness, the yen holds at 150+ and the US tariff cost is passed through in price. The value-chain mix and the completed Americas distribution restructuring hold adjusted OP margin at 11-11.5%, close to the FY2024 peak, and revenue compounds ~3.5% a year. Buybacks continue at the H1 FY2027 pace (not modelled in the count, value-neutral under the flat-count convention).
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027 H2 disappoints as Middle East logistics disruption, tariffs and a yen rally toward 140 bite; FY2028-29 is a genuine downturn like FY2020-21 (revenue -10%, -6%) with coal and iron-ore miners deferring fleet replacement and North American housing/infrastructure softening. Adjusted OP margin troughs near 5%, EBITDA at 10%, D&A and fixed costs deleverage, and working capital releases only partly offset the earnings fall. Recovery is slow and the mid-cycle margin settles at 14% EBITDA (adjusted OP ~9%) rather than 15% as tariff and rebrand costs stick. Net debt of 369bn plus 75bn of leases is serviceable throughout - this is an earnings-cycle bear case, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because FY2027 is a near-peak year on a weak yen, and the main downside drivers (yen reversion, mining commodity weakness, US tariffs, Middle East logistics) are correlated macro risks the company itself flags; it is a cyclical bear case, not a solvency one, so not higher. Bull cut to 25% because it needs North American demand, copper/gold mining capex, the FX rate and tariff pass-through to all hold simultaneously through FY2029.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a cyclical on mid-cycle cash flow, not on the guided peak year: anchor FY2027 to guidance, force a correction into the explicit years, capitalise a 15% EBITDA margin (adjusted OP ~10%) at a 15x FCF cap, and charge every claim once - leases as debt in the bridge, minorities as an 11.5% leakage in the flows, equity-method stakes added at book because their income is excluded. House and street coincide because SBC is ~0%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Peak-earnings extrapolation: FY2027 guidance (adjusted OP 10.3%) is near the top of a 4-12% cycle; a 1pp change in the mid-cycle EBITDA margin moves base IV by roughly JPY 500/share.
FX: revenue is ~75% overseas and guidance assumes JPY 154/USD; a 10% yen appreciation cuts JPY revenue and margin materially.
Mining capex cycle: ~30% of revenue; coal and iron-ore demand already weakening, copper/gold carrying the segment.
US tariffs and the Americas distribution restructuring (Deere dealer exit) - cost and execution risk in the #1 growth region.
Working-capital intensity: ~42% of revenue in net operating working capital; the model assumes 30% capture, and a return to the FY2019/FY2023 inventory builds would wipe out a year of FCF.
Terminal cap: 15x FCF binds in all scenarios; at the Gordon value (18.5x) base IV would be ~15% higher - the cap is a deliberate cyclical haircut.
NCI leakage folded into the tax rate (40.5%): if minority-held subsidiaries (Tata Hitachi, China) shrink relative to the group the leakage falls and value rises.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (query1.finance.yahoo.com, 6305.T) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4,312-7,225.
data_sources.financials: Kessan tanshin (English): 6305.T_Annual_FY2025.txt (year ended 31 Mar 2026: income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, FY2027 initial guidance) and 6305.T_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (six months to 30 Sep 2026: balance sheet for net debt, leases, NCI, equity-method investments, treasury shares; revised FY2027 guidance). History from 6305.T_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and the kpis table (AdjustedOperatingProfit, Depreciation, CashTaxesPaid, MiningRevenue, ValueChainRevenue).
data_sources.qualitative: Outlook sections of the FY2025 annual and H1 FY2027 tanshin (demand by region and mineral, FX assumptions, tariffs, LANDCROS rebrand, dividend JPY 190).
